transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alejandra Cruz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nora Liu (Redwood CSM), Rajesh Iyer (Quantiva VP Eng), Maya Thompson (Quantiva SRE), Liam O'Connor (Quantiva PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through interim mitigations and proposed Dedicated pilot. Quantiva asked for repro harness and wanted clarification on KV cache eviction reasons and how batching changes affect tail latency. Agreed action owners and timeline.

--- Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, every ~30s snippets, transcription has small errors) ---
00:00 Alejandra: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're aiming to go 50 minutes today, run through the postmortem points and lock owners. Quick check, Maya, Rajesh, you seeing the calendar invite?
00:07 Maya: Yeah, I see it. Sorry ran a tiny bit late, had to pull a redis trace.
00:11 Rajesh: All good.
00:14 Alejandra: Cool. Quick recap — last Tuesday's token-throttle spikes, we saw steady-state throughput then sudden eviction waves, which pushed a bunch of requests into fallback and spiked 95th pct latency to ~1.2s. Today we want to cover root cause hypothesis, repro plan, and the playbook integration. Samir, you want to pick up the tech rundown?
00:29 Samir: Sure. So to be clear there are two related symptoms: one is KV cache churn on long-tail keys, and second is batching threshold oscillation when sequences hit the weird length distribution. The churn seems correlated with prefix invalidation from their upstream cache warmer — or maybe a misconfigured LRU in their sidecar.
00:48 Maya: Can I interrupt — when you say prefix invalidation, are you meaning our prefix/KV cache or their own app-level cache? We only invalidated explicitly during deploys last week.
00:57 Samir: Good call. We're seeing invalidation signals in the proxy traces that line up with a sidecar TTL 0 event, which suggests the app-level warmers are doing an aggressive expire. That then increases requests that miss the KV, causing longer token generation and more concurrent KV allocations, which pushes memory pressure and triggers eviction in the runtime.
01:20 Rajesh: Right, we pushed a change to the warming script to reduce stale embeddings last Wednesday. Might be related. We didn't think it would affect inference KV at all but could be.
01:27 Nora: (whispers) sometimes names are reversed in the traces so word alignment is messy.
01:31 Alejandra: That's fine — the traces aren't perfect. Samir, what do we need from Quantiva to repro locally?
01:36 Samir: The ideal is a 30-60 minute traffic slice with request bodies (anonymized) and the trace IDs for the slow windows. If you can include the sidecar config and the warming job logs that would be super helpful. We can run the eviction stress harness against that.
01:52 Maya: We can do that. We'll scrub PII. I'll put the slice in s3 and share link.
01:57 Liam: Quick question: if the root cause is the sidecar TTL, why didn't the fallback route kick earlier? It seemed to cascade into other services.
02:05 Samir: Two things. One, the fallback route existed but was on a soft threshold — it only engages after a certain queue depth. Two, during the eviction wave multiple replicas hit the threshold at similar times so the fallback logic experienced a stampede and then the global circuit opened, routing to lower capacity variants and pushing latency further.
02:27 Rajesh: So it's an amplification effect.
02:28 Samir: Exactly.
02:30 Alejandra: That points to two immediate mitigations — tighten the fallback threshold to a more conservative level, and add jittered circuit engagement to avoid stampedes. We recommended those in the interim patch.
02:40 Rajesh: On thresholds — what's the risk to cost/latency if we engage earlier? Our product team is worried about over-falling back and increasing tail queries to a cheaper but lower-quality model.
02:50 Alejandra: Tradeoff: earlier fallback reduces 95/99 latency but can increase per-request cost (if routing to Dedicated or replica with higher per-token units) and may reduce generation quality depending on variant. We'll quantify in the pilot.
03:02 Maya: Can we have a quick explanation of Dedicated pilot idea? We've seen Dedicated described in docs but want specific config for this scenario.
03:10 Alejandra: Yes. The pilot is a constrained Dedicated pool with pinned model variant, controlled autoscaling and a conservative batching policy. The aims are: reproduce the eviction under realistic load, validate the jittered fallback, and measure token-level cost with the new hysteresis thresholds. We'll provide config templates.
03:26 Samir: Also we can instrument continuous KV cache metrics and expose a metric for 'KV churn rate' to trigger automations.
03:33 Maya: That metric would be helpful. We have a custom telemetry pipeline — we'll map it.
03:38 Liam: When you say 'pinned model variant' what exactly will change? Quantiva uses our LLM v3 quantized endpoint in prod.
03:45 Samir: For the pilot we recommend using same model architecture but a variant with slightly smaller KV footprint — quantized 7b-int4 style — to reduce memory pressure, plus an alternate kernel selection that reduces ephemeral allocations. We'll profile both.
03:58 Rajesh: Are there functional regressions with that variant?
04:01 Samir: Small, usually subtle hallucination/fluency tradeoffs on long-form generative tasks. For our use-case if you need deterministic summarization there might be edge effects; we'll capture evals.
04:11 Maya: We care more about latency and correctness for classification-ish flows. Summaries are lower priority.
04:16 Alejandra: Good context. We'll run the pilot focusing on your high-priority flows.
04:19 Nora: (note) we should loop in Security on data handling for the s3 traces.
04:23 Rajesh: Yes, expect me to cc security. I also wanted clarity on the runbook changes — can you summarize what you propose?
04:31 Alejandra: Sure. Proposed runbook updates: 1) Rapid detection alert for KV churn > threshold; 2) Auto-apply fallback with jittered engagement; 3) Graceful scale-up policy to add warm replicas before circuit opens; 4) Post-incident telemetry capture including stack dumps for top latency traces.
04:49 Liam: On #3, how quick is warm replica spin-up? Our concern is cold starts.
04:54 Samir: With our Dedicated pools we have pre-warmed capacity options; warm spin-up is ~45-90s depending on image size. That's why we recommended small buffer capacity on Dedicated pilot so scale-up is fast enough to avoid triggering full fallback.
05:09 Maya: Ok. If warm is 45-90s that helps. We'll need to coordinate scaling alarms in our paging policy.
05:14 Alejandra: Absolutely. We'll produce alarm docs.
05:17 Rajesh: A practical question — we noticed some mis-labeled trace spans in the Fireflies export last week; are your trace ids stable across versions?
05:26 Samir: Trace ids are stable but sometimes the instrumented labels change after runtime updates. We'll include a mapping doc in the trace package.
05:34 Maya: Great.
05:36 [10m mark - side conversation about calendar scheduling and a quick sync between Nora and Liam about decision owners]
15:05 Rajesh: For repro, do you need the exact traffic header shapes (user-agent, session ids)?
15:11 Samir: Session ids are fine to hash/anonymize. User-agent we need only if you suspect routing differences. The body and token lengths matter most.
15:21 Maya: We'll scrub PII and provide hash keys.
15:24 Alejandra: We'll also provide a small harness script to replay the slice against a local runtime and a cloud Dedicated cluster. Samir will coordinate.
15:32 Samir: Plan: step 1 run local repro within a docker image using their traffic slice and their sidecar config; step 2 escalate to internal stress harness that pushes concurrency and watches KV churn and eviction rate; step 3 spin Dedicated pilot to validate mitigations.
15:46 Liam: Are there known mitigations for LRU thrashing besides changing sidecar TTL?
15:50 Samir: Yes — prefix-aware caching, sticky affinity to keep hot keys on same replica, and adaptive batching windows that favor lower concurrency. There's also quantization of KV entries to reduce footprint. Each has tradeoffs.
16:06 Rajesh: Sticky affinity sounds promising but we have multi-AZ routing — might complicate things.
16:13 Samir: It's an engineering lift but possible as a soft layer in the service mesh. We'll prototype in the pilot.
16:18 Maya: Anything on security/compliance for the Dedicated pilot? We need to make sure keys and traces don't leave our region.
16:25 Alejandra: We can run Dedicated in your preferred cloud region and use customer-managed KMS for keys. We'll include the security checklist and earliest SOC2 artifacts.
16:36 Rajesh: Good. Also, what about alert fatigue — tightening fallback might increase alerts. We want a conservative approach to avoid noisy paging.
16:45 Alejandra: We'll suggest combined alerting: only page on sustained KV-churn + 95th latency beyond threshold for >3m to avoid flappers.
16:55 Liam: Cool.
17:00 Samir: Quick note: we found in preliminary logs that when sequence length spikes above ~1,200 tokens the batching optimizer chooses a different kernel, which uses more scratch memory and increases ephemeral allocations — that coincides with the eviction windows. So there's a kernel selection angle too.
17:19 Maya: Is kernel selector tunable?
17:23 Samir: Yes, there are flags we can set per deployment to force a specific kernel path, at the cost of average throughput. We'll test that in pilot.
17:31 Rajesh: I want to ensure the pilot results are actionable — can you give us a short deck with key metrics and suggested SLO adjustments after the benchmark?
17:38 Alejandra: We'll deliver a 1-page deck + a deeper trace notebook. The 1-pager will include recommended SLO adjustments and cost delta.
17:46 Nora: Add to that the rollback criteria for any SLO change so it's reversible.
17:50 Alejandra: Good call.
17:53 [Silence while someone scribbles notes]
18:00 Maya: For timelines — we can share the 24h traffic slice by Wed 2026-05-06. Security sign-off may add a day.
18:07 Samir: We'll aim to run local repro immediately on receipt and share initial findings by 2026-05-08. Dedicated benchmark week of 2026-05-12 pending pilot approvals.
18:18 Rajesh: Sounds reasonable.
18:21 Liam: One last question — can you demonstrate the jittered fallback logic in a short video or gif? Product would like to see the UX.
18:29 Alejandra: Yes, we can record a 3-5 minute demo of the fallback engagement and the circuit jitter. We'll attach to the deck.
18:36 Maya: Great.
18:38 [Wrap-up]
18:40 Alejandra: Recap of next steps: Samir runs repro and uploads results; Maya shares trimmed logs + sidecar config; Alejandra shares pricing/pilot docs and 1-pager. We'll schedule the Dedicated benchmark and follow up with Security. Any objections?
18:55 Rajesh: No objections. Thanks all.
18:58 Liam: Thanks.
19:00 Meeting ends.
